Our approach
01 / Process

We didn't restyle the site. We rebuilt the thinking, then the structure, then the surface.

We treated the brief as raw material — strong on substance, but it never said who the site is for. So we started there, and let every later decision follow from it.

The starting point
01 / Process
Earlier concept · v0

This is where a faithful reading of the brief lands.

An early, deliberately brief-faithful concept from the team. It renders exactly what the brief says — which is what makes it a useful reference: it shows the ceiling of a literal reading.

The right instincts are already here — the navy & yellow system, the window-onto-Armenia aperture, the ambition of a "We know Armenia" hero. We kept those. Here's why we didn't stop here.

What was already strong
Credit first

The raw material — and the instincts — were strong.

From the brief
  • Two service lines — Research & Advisory + LARP. A real, unusual differentiator.
  • The portfolio — dated, named-client, method-tagged projects. Gold-standard proof.
  • Impact metrics — 25+ years · 150+ projects · 30+ experts · nationwide.
  • The collective story — and "fieldwork becomes adventure."
From the v0 concept
  • The window-onto-Armenia aperture device.
  • The navy & yellow colour system.
  • The "We know Armenia" hero ambition.
  • A connector-bar and geometric-line instinct.

What was missing wasn't taste — it was the strategy and the proof. We kept the instincts and did the homework.

Where a literal reading falls short — 2 of 3
The structure hides the client path

"The navigation works against the sale."

What v0 shows
P1 "Work with us" kept in the primary nav. A procurement-minded buyer never clicks a careers-sounding link — the client pitch is hidden behind it.
P3 Service names drift right on the page: "Market & Consumer Insights", "Policy Analysis & Strategic Advisory", three different LARP sub-items. It reads as careless to a standards-driven reader.
What the redesign does
D8 Split the two jobs. A client path (Services · Our Work · Contact) and a separate Careers track. "Work with us" is retired.
D12 One canonical name per service, used identically in nav, URLs and copy — the taxonomy stops competing with itself.
Theme→the buyer's path is made obvious, and the details read as rigorous.
Where a literal reading falls short — 3 of 3
An SEO team would have to restart

"Nothing's ready for launch or growth."

These gaps a screenshot can't show — they're structural. They don't cost a visitor today; they cost the site the moment anyone tries to build on it.

P5

No SEO-ready foundations

Undefined URLs, no one-topic-per-page logic, no metadata slots. An SEO team would have to restructure before starting.

P7

Insights, orphaned

A menu item marked "hidden, not active," never specified — a dead-link risk with no roadmap behind it.

P4

Contact left blank

Phone, email and address are placeholders in the brief — and contact is the one action the whole site exists to drive.

Discovery · Phase 1
The decision that reorganizes everything

The brief never named an audience.

The portfolio answers the question for us: it is overwhelmingly international. So the site is optimised to win the research manager or evaluation lead vetting a local partner in Armenia.

D1Primary audience = international organisations & donors. Others are served, not dropped.
Primary — the evidence
World Bank·UNICEF·OECD·EU·EBRD·ADB·UNHCR·OSCE·MCC
Secondary

Private sector & government / public bodies

Distinct track

Talent — the collective, on its own path

Discovery · Phase 1
Procurement-minded · risk-averse

This buyer won't be won by mood.

They're vetting a partner for a tender. Five things decide it — and every one is evidence, which is why proof has to surface early.

01

Rigour

Sampling, CAPI/CATI/qual, multi-level QC, ethics.

02

Field capacity

Nationwide reach, sample scale, ability to prime.

03

Track record

Named clients, dated, comparable engagements.

04

Local access

The thing they cannot get in-house — real knowledge of Armenia.

05

Reliability

Deadlines met across a multi-phase programme.

Discovery · Phase 1
Tone of voice · D2

Human at the frame. Rigorous in the substance.

The evocative lines earn attention at hero and section openers; the exact, evidence-led voice carries the service copy, the methods, the numbers.

Warmth earns attention; the evidence converts it. Used the other way around, we'd bore the visitor or fail the credibility test.

Before — the brief's voice
"Since 2001, Media Model has been helping organizations model the way from complexity to clarity through research, analysis, and advisory."
After — the blend
"We know Armenia. Since 2001 we've helped organisations turn that knowledge into decisions — through research, evaluation and advisory grounded in two decades of nationwide fieldwork."

The new architecture · Phase 2
Discoverable and complete — not dominant
D10

Position LARP right.

Land acquisition & resettlement is a rare, full-cycle capability — a genuine differentiator for government and IFI buyers.

So it's a co-equal service line with its own page and portfolio filter — but it does not take equal share of the homepage, which stays optimised for the research buyer.

Leads

On its own /services/larp/ page, the government path, and IFI infrastructure searches.

Supports

On the homepage, as one of two clear service lines — present, not dominant.

This sets up the prototype's deliberate two-section treatment.

The new architecture · Phase 2
Consistency & future-proofing

Four quieter fixes that make the site read as careful.

D12
One name per service
Market & Consumer Insights  →  Market & Consumer Research
Policy Analysis & Strategic Advisory  →  Policy Analysis & Advisory
One canonical name across nav, URLs and copy.
D13
About, tightened

Our Philosophy folds into Our Story; Our Impact splits — metrics stay in About, the portfolio moves to Our Work. Four thin pages become one coherent story.

D11
Insights, reserved

URL and template slot kept for a future thought-leadership layer — but out of nav, with no orphaned link.

D15
SEO-ready foundations

Clean URLs, one topic per page, metadata slots, crawlable linking — a structure an SEO team can build on without restructuring. Readiness, not a keyword strategy.

Visual direction · Phase 4
Reuniting the identity with the site

Two references, pulling opposite ways.

The agency campaign is bold and poster-like — navy/yellow blocks, silhouettes, slab headlines. The editorial web references are restrained and premium — airy off-white, oversized type, quiet air.

The idea that resolves it: a restrained editorial canvas carrying bold, recurring brand beats.

Why this, strategically

The airy canvas is the credibility spine the donor audience needs. The boldness returns as rhythm, not wallpaper.

bold beat→breathe→bold beat

Credibility before persuasion; accents, not wallpaper.

The payoff · the built homepage
Same instinct, finally delivered
v0 · mood-only hero
v1 · the built hero

The same window-onto-Armenia instinct — a black void and a dead aperture become a portal-zoom that opens onto the real valley, resolving to "We know Armenia" and one clear CTA. It lands hardest because you already know v0.
